does: Presses a clove of garlic flat under the blade of a knife, or under a pestle, and works it with salt into a damp, rough paste that melts into a dressing or a sauce.

intro.what: Garlic is pressed and worked with salt into a damp paste for a dressing or sauce.
intro.why: Changing pieces into paste lets the garlic disperse rather than remain as distinct chopped fragments.

how: Peel the clove and set it on a board with a little salt. The salt grips it and wears it down.
Lay the flat of a broad knife on the clove and press down with the heel of the hand until it splits.
Drag the blade over the pieces with the flat tilted, again and again, until the garlic is a damp paste with no lumps.
Scrape the paste into the dressing or the sauce and stir it in at once.

cues.text: The garlic turns from pieces to a pale, glossy, wet paste.
A sharp, raw scent rises as soon as it breaks, and fades into the dressing.

mistakes.mistake: Crushing without salt, so that the garlic slides about under the blade and stays in pieces.
mistakes.fix: Add a little salt first, so that it grips.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the paste on the board to turn bitter and harsh.
mistakes.fix: Stir it into the acid or the oil soon after it is done.

quiz.question: Why make garlic into paste for this method?
choices: So it stays in firm separate cubes.
So it disperses into the dressing or sauce.
So the cloves keep their whole shape.
quiz.because: A damp paste combines with the liquid more readily than intact pieces.

quiz.question: What role does salt play during crushing here?
choices: It keeps the garlic sliding freely.
It keeps the garlic pieces firm while only the juices spread.
It helps grip and abrade the garlic.
quiz.because: Salt provides grip and abrasion while the garlic is worked down.

quiz.question: Which appearance shows the intended result?
choices: A pale damp paste without lumps.
Dry intact cloves with split skins.
Large firm cubes on a wet board.
quiz.because: The visible pieces should have been worked into a cohesive wet paste.

quiz.question: Garlic slides around and remains in pieces. What should change?
choices: Polish the board with oil first.
Work it with salt as this method describes.
Keep pressing intact cloves without working them.
quiz.because: Salt helps prevent sliding while the garlic is worn into paste.

variant_of.differs: The garlic is pressed and dragged flat under a blade or a pestle for a few moments into a damp, rough paste, and not worked long in a mortar until it is smooth.
